gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Dabbsson 1000L (1,008 Wh, 24 lb, 0.2 lb heavier than the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2) costs $386 at Dabbsson's US store on 2026-11-14. That makes it the cheapest unit of about 1 kWh within a pound of the lightest, at $163 less than the $549.99 that ChatGPT's own runner-up, the Anker C1000 Gen 2, was shown at.
standout_why: I opened backup-power.org (cited), solarpowerauditor.com camping (cited), practicalbuyerguide.com (cited) and juicebench.com (cited once). None of them mentions the Dabbsson 1000L at all. One ChatGPT answer listed the 1000L at 24.0 lb in a table but gave no price. The rival pages price only the five usual models (Explorer 1000 v2, C1000 Gen 2, Elite 100 V2, DELTA 3 Plus, AC180), and their prices are list prices or dated Sep 5 to Nov 6. Only juicebench lists the OUPES Exodus 1200 (10.5 kg). It gives no chemistry, and it doesn't say the unit is sold out.
decides: The lightest pick stays the same. The Explorer 1000 v2 still has the best Wh per lb (1,070 / 23.8 = 45.0), and the only lighter units are under 1,000 Wh (OUPES Exodus 1200, 992 Wh, sold out) or the HomePower 1000 v2, whose black version is sold out. What changes is the value runner-up. ChatGPT named the Anker C1000 Gen 2 (24.9 lb, about $549.99) as the second choice. The Dabbsson 1000L is 0.9 lb lighter than the Anker and $164 cheaper, at $0.38 per Wh. It loses only if you need more than 1,200 W of AC output (Anker 2,000 W, Jackery 1,500 W).
